skill.name: writing-to-logseq
skill.description: Write structured pages, blocks, properties, tags, and conversation notes to Logseq DB graphs through the Logseq HTTP API.
skill.summary: Writes structured content to Logseq using the local HTTP API.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most external-command and blocker detections are false positives caused by markdown code fences, inline function names, or safety guidance text. The executable script does make authenticated HTTP requests to a local or configured Logseq API and reads the Logseq token from environment or config. No prompt-injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Destructive operations can remove Logseq graph data.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation, dry-run support, or backup guidance before delete_page and delete_block are used.

remediation.issue: A configured API URL can receive the bearer token.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before non-loopback URLs are used and document that LOGSEQ_API_URL must point to a trusted Logseq API.

remediation.issue: The Logseq API token is read from environment variables or local config.
remediation.suggestion: Document token handling clearly and advise users not to store tokens in shared project files.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Logseq Write Operations
semantic_findings.description: The skill exposes delete_page and delete_block operations that can remove user Logseq data. The script checks existence first, but deletion still mutates the user graph.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The delete methods directly call Logseq deletePage and removeBlock after resolving the target. This is intended functionality, but it carries clear data-loss risk.

semantic_findings.title: Configurable API Endpoint Can Receive Token
semantic_findings.description: The writer accepts LOGSEQ_API_URL or config file URL overrides and sends the bearer token to that endpoint. This supports custom setups but could expose the token if the endpoint is untrusted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The URL and token are loaded from environment or config, then the token is placed in the Authorization header. Risk depends on user configuration, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.user_title: Write Notes and Blocks to Logseq
content.value_statement: Capturing work in Logseq is slow when notes, tasks, and properties must be created manually. This skill writes structured pages and blocks through the Logseq HTTP API.
actual_capabilities: Creates Logseq pages with initial content and properties.
Adds, appends, updates, and deletes Logseq blocks.
Sets, updates, and removes block properties.
Adds or removes tags on existing blocks.
Syncs conversation notes into timestamped Logseq pages.
Provides safety guidance and reusable page templates.
limitations: Requires the Logseq HTTP API to be enabled.
Requires a valid Logseq API token.
Can modify or delete graph data when instructed.
Does not provide a built-in backup or rollback system.

use_cases.title: Capture Research Notes
use_cases.description: Create pages for sources, summaries, tags, and follow-up questions without manual Logseq entry.

use_cases.title: Turn Meetings Into Tasks
use_cases.description: Write meeting summaries, action items, priorities, and status properties directly into a team knowledge graph.

use_cases.title: Archive AI Sessions
use_cases.description: Save Claude, Codex, or Claude Code conversation summaries as timestamped Logseq pages.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Logseq page named Project Inbox with a short overview and three empty task blocks.

prompt_templates.title: Append Meeting Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Add new content to an existing page
prompt_templates.prompt: Append these meeting notes to the Logseq page Team Sync and tag the new block as Meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Set Properties and Tags
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this Logseq block with status In Progress, priority High, and tags Project and Review.

prompt_templates.title: Sync a Conversation Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a timestamped Claude Notes page for this session with summary, decisions, action items, and related pages.

output_examples.input: Create a Logseq page for a product planning meeting.
output: A new meeting page is created with date, attendees, agenda, notes, and action item sections.
The page includes properties for type, status, and follow-up owner.

output_examples.input: Save this AI conversation summary to Logseq.
output: A timestamped Claude Notes page is created or updated.
The summary, decisions, and follow-up questions are added as structured blocks.

output_examples.input: Mark a task block as complete and add a Review tag.
output_examples.output: The selected block is updated with the requested status property and tag while preserving its existing content.

best_practices: Use append or get-or-create operations for repeatable workflows.
Confirm page titles and block UUIDs before updates or deletes.
Test large write workflows in a separate Logseq graph first.
anti_patterns: Do not run bulk deletes without confirmation and a backup.
Do not store Logseq API tokens in shared repository files.
Do not point LOGSEQ_API_URL at an untrusted endpoint.

faq.question: Does this skill require Logseq to be open?
faq.answer: Yes. Logseq must be running with the HTTP API enabled and reachable.

faq.question: Where does the API token come from?
faq.answer: The script reads LOGSEQ_API_TOKEN from the environment or a local Logseq skill config file.

faq.question: Can this skill delete Logseq data?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes page and block delete operations, so users should confirm targets before deletion.

faq.question: Does it send notes to the internet?
faq.answer: The default endpoint is local loopback. A custom LOGSEQ_API_URL can change the destination.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it import an entire existing vault?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on writing pages, blocks, properties, tags, and conversation notes through the Logseq API.
